'''Harald Ganzinger''' (31 October 1950, [[Werneck]] – 3 June 2004, [[Saarbrücken]]) was a German [[computer scientist]] who together with [[Leo Bachmair]] developed the [[superposition calculus]], which is (as of 2007) used in most of the state-of-the-art [[automated theorem prover]]s for [[first-order logic]].

He received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from the [[Technical University of Munich]] in 1978. Before 1991 he was a Professor of Computer Science at [[Technical University of Dortmund|University of Dortmund]]. Then he joined the [[Max Planck Institute for Computer Science]] in [[Saarbrücken]] shortly after it was founded in 1991. Until 2004 he was the Director of the Programming Logics department of the [[Max Planck Institute for Computer Science]] and honorary professor at [[Saarland University]]. His research group created the [[SPASS theorem prover|SPASS]] [[automated theorem prover]].

He received the [[Herbrand Award]] in 2004 ([[Posthumous recognition|posthumous]]) for his important contributions to [[automated theorem proving]].
